subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed cross-product localization contract, including the fixed 21-locale v1 set and release-visible completeness gates?
rationale: The proposal creates permanent shared contracts and ownership obligations across Gateway errors, recipient locale state, command and plugin metadata, and release policy; those boundaries cannot be approved through mechanical review.

options.title: Continue scoped RFC review
options.body: Keep the draft open, resolve each owner decision, and narrow disputed contracts before acceptance.

options.title: Accept the full direction
options.body: Approve the shared runtime, metadata, coverage, and release-gating model as the implementation target.

options.title: Limit runtime scope
options.body: Restrict RFC 0024 to locale resolution and structured runtime messages, deferring metadata and completeness gates to later RFCs.

recommendation.title: Continue scoped RFC review
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open, resolve each owner decision, and narrow disputed contracts before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-product architecture and release-policy choice, and the available project guidance identifies steipete as the strongest top-level decision owner.
